The concentration of the $N_2O_5$ is tracked over time, and the results are plotted on the graph above. Based on the graph, what are the possible units of the rate constant for this reaction?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph shows [N2O5] on the vertical axis and Time (s) on the horizontal axis. The concentration starts near 1.0 at time 0 and decreases in a curved, exponential-like way. From the plotted curve, [N2O5] falls to about 0.50 after roughly the first few seconds and to about 0.25 after a roughly comparable additional time interval. Reasoning: Similar successive half-lives indicate first-order decomposition. For a first-order reaction, rate = k[N2O5], so the rate constant k has units of inverse time. Since the graph uses seconds for time, the possible units of k are s^-1.
